entities.summary: Domenico Guidi was a prominent Italian Baroque sculptor. Born in unknown, Guidi studied under Giuseppe Maria Corsi and worked closely with Gian Lorenzo Bernini. Guidi's most notable works include the bronze statue of the Emperor Augustus for the Villa Albani, showcasing his mastery of classical forms. His sculptures often featured intricate details and emotive expressions, setting a new standard for Baroque art. Guidi's innovative style influenced future generations of artists, including the French Rococo movement. His legacy can be seen in the works of artists such as Jean-Antoine Houdon and Jacques-Louis David. Guidi's death in 1701 marked the end of an era, but his art continued to inspire and captivate audiences for centuries to come.
